VO and multilayer perceptron (MLP) retentions jointly correct 25-81% of pretrained errors, demonstrating overlapping recovered behavior, which we call operational redundancy. Third, removing semantically selected directions reduces VO-retained recovery more than matched-random removal in all five settings. Together, these results distinguish semantic alignment, removal cost, and retained recovery as complementary evidence about the functional role of fine-tuning updates within the evaluated CLIP recipe.
authors: Chih-Ting Liao, Kezhen Bao, Xin Cao
bullets: Fine-tuned CLIP models are evaluated on synthetic financial charts, Flowers102, EuroSAT, and FGVCAircraft using ViT-L/14, plus Flowers102 with ViT-B/16.
Attention value-output (VO) updates alone recover 43–87% of the accuracy improvement, though reverting them does not change chart accuracy.
VO updates recover more loss improvement than matched random subsets across all evaluated settings.
VO and MLP retentions jointly correct 25–81% of pretrained errors, indicating operational redundancy in recovered behavior.
Removing semantically selected directions harms VO-retained recovery more than matched-random removal in all five settings.
papers.selection_reason: Analyzes functional content in CLIP fine-tuning deltas, relevant to understanding multimodal foundation model behavior.
papers.title: Reversion, Retention, and Semantic Intervention: Measuring Functional Content in CLIP Fine-Tuning Deltas
papers.tldr: The study uses reversion and retention tests to measure which semantically identified CLIP fine-tuning updates functionally support task adaptation, revealing substantial but overlapping roles for attention VO and MLP updates.

papers.abstract: Open-vocabulary 3D occupancy prediction is important for embodied agents operating in complex environments whose semantic categories extend beyond fixed taxonomies. While recent studies have explored open-vocabulary occupancy in outdoor driving scenarios, indoor environments remain challenging due to dense occlusions, complex geometry, and fine-grained long-tailed semantics. To reduce the need for expensive voxel-level semantic annotations, we study a geometry-only supervision setting requiring only binary occupancy labels. We build upon Language-Embedded Gaussians as a unified representation coupling 3D geometry with language-aligned semantics. For geometry learning, we introduce an opacity-aware Poisson-based Gaussian-to-Occupancy formulation that enables stable volumetric aggregation under binary occupancy supervision. For semantic learning, we render Gaussian features into images and align them with a frozen open-vocabulary model, together with Progressive Temperature Decay to reduce feature mixing during Gaussian splatting. Building on this framework, we further introduce Instance-Level Semantic Consistency to alleviate fragmented object predictions, and Covisibility-Aware Support-View Selection to provide informative and less redundant multi-view semantic supervision. We also extend our framework to outdoor driving scenarios to evaluate its generality across substantially different environments. Extensive experiments on indoor and outdoor benchmarks demonstrate that our method achieves strong open-vocabulary occupancy performance, validating the effectiveness and generality of our framework. Code will be available at https://github.com/JuIvyy/LegoOcc.
authors: Changqing Zhou, Yueru Luo, Han Zhang, Zeyu Jiang, Changhao Chen
bullets: Targets indoor and outdoor scenes with dense occlusions, complex geometry, and long-tailed semantics beyond fixed taxonomies.
Uses binary occupancy labels for geometry, with an opacity-aware Poisson Gaussian-to-occupancy formulation for stable volumetric aggregation.
Aligns rendered Gaussian features with a frozen open-vocabulary model and applies Progressive Temperature Decay to reduce feature mixing.
Introduces Instance-Level Semantic Consistency and Covisibility-Aware Support-View Selection to improve fragmented and redundant multi-view predictions.
Experiments on indoor and outdoor benchmarks show strong performance and cross-environment generality.
papers.selection_reason: Open-vocabulary 3D occupancy prediction couples geometry with language-aligned semantics, fitting 3D perception and spatial understanding.
papers.title: LegoOcc++: Towards Consistent Open-Vocabulary 3D Occupancy Prediction
papers.tldr: LegoOcc++ enables open-vocabulary 3D occupancy prediction from geometry-only supervision by combining language-aligned Gaussian representations with consistency-aware semantic learning.

papers.abstract: Robot tasks require grounding spatial language in physical scenes, but task success alone cannot establish whether spatial instructions are followed. We present BEHAVIOR-Spatial, a benchmark built on BEHAVIOR-1K that measures spatial question answering, point-based target grounding, and robot action to examine how VLM spatial understanding relates to VLA behavior. It comprises 3,256 spatial questions across 49 activities, 1,240 grounding queries across 14 manipulation tasks, and action evaluations covering those 14 tasks and 10 navigation tasks. Our manipulation protocol evaluates held-out configurations and instruction following when the requested target changes within a fixed training layout. The baseline achieves 41.6% on held-out configurations but only 16.1% under changed instructions. VLM adaptation and robot-data pretraining provide limited improvements, whereas oracle visual target cues raise these rates to 60.3% and 38.0%, respectively. Perception evaluations reveal policy-dependent correlations between VLM question-answering and grounding accuracy and VLA manipulation performance. Together, these findings motivate evaluating spatial instruction following alongside task completion and examining when spatial perception performance translates into robot behavior. Project website: https://arielchen07.github.io/behavior-spatial/.
authors: Sirui Chen, Huang Huang, Qineng Wang, Wenlong Huang, Manling Li, Ruohan Zhang, Li Fei-Fei, Jiajun Wu
bullets: Benchmarks spatial question answering, point-based target grounding, and robot actions on BEHAVIOR-1K.
Includes 3,256 spatial questions, 1,240 grounding queries, 14 manipulation tasks, and 10 navigation tasks.
Tests held-out scene configurations and target changes under fixed training layouts.
Baseline action success drops from 41.6% on held-out configurations to 16.1% with changed instructions; oracle visual cues improve both settings.
Shows that perception accuracy does not consistently translate into robot behavior, motivating joint evaluation of spatial understanding and task completion.
papers.selection_reason: Benchmark linking VLM spatial understanding to VLA behavior in manipulation and navigation; fits spatial intelligence and embodied robotics.
papers.title: Behavior Spatial Benchmark: Evaluating Spatial Understanding for Robotics
papers.tldr: BEHAVIOR-Spatial evaluates whether vision-language models and robot policies truly understand and follow spatial instructions in physical scenes.

papers.abstract: LVLM benchmarks tell us whether a model answers correctly, but not which visual conventions it has retained, nor where those conventions live. Sketches expose this hidden structure. A sketch removes texture, lighting, and photographic context while preserving the strokes humans judged sufficient for recognition. If an LVLM can operate on that abstraction, the surviving signal is structural rather than merely photometric. We introduce a training-free sketch probe with three readouts: temporal part-construction order, spatial attention-based grounding, and the mechanistic layer/head locus of grounding. We evaluate nine LVLMs on part order and five on the attention readouts, over two part-annotated sketch datasets. Three findings emerge. First, LVLM part order tracks human convention: models reproduce canonical orderings where human drawings converge, and become correspondingly variable where human orderings vary. Controls that blank, withhold, and mismatch the sketch locate this convention in the language model. Second, part-level grounding survives the abstraction: attention heads selected from the frozen model with an existing recipe recover part and object regions on object and scene sketches, with no grounding supervision. Third, the grounding signal concentrates in a narrow mid-network band whose location follows the base language model rather than parameter count in the two families we compare, and remains stable across object and scene sketches. The result is a practical diagnostic for sketch-driven LVLMs: no fine-tuning, no auxiliary segmenter, and a layer band that doubles as a head-selection prior, matching or improving grounding mAcc@0.1 in every model and dataset we tested.
authors: Chaitat Utintu, Ahmed Bourouis, Arkaprabha Basu, Yi-Zhe Song
bullets: Introduces a training-free sketch probe measuring temporal part order, spatial grounding, and the mechanistic layer/head location of grounding.
Across nine LVLMs, part-construction order follows human conventions: canonical where people agree and variable where human order varies.
Across five LVLMs, attention-based grounding recovers object and part regions from object and scene sketches without grounding supervision.
Grounding concentrates in a stable mid-network layer band tied to the base language model rather than parameter count in the studied families.
The probe matches or improves grounding mAcc@0.1 in every tested model and dataset, without fine-tuning or an auxiliary segmenter.
papers.selection_reason: Probes LVLM visual conventions, grounding, and localization, contributing to multimodal foundation model analysis.
papers.title: What Sketches Tell Us about LVLMs: Conventions, Grounding, and Localisation
papers.tldr: Sketches reveal that LVLMs retain human-like visual conventions and part-level grounding, with grounding concentrated in a narrow, language-model-dependent mid-network band.

papers.abstract: People have long dreamed of an assistant that is always there to guide them and remind what they forget, from new dishes to lost keys. Powered by multimodal large language models (MLLMs), egocentric AI assistants on wearable devices are bringing this dream within reach: they see what the user sees and give instructions for user's physical work when necessary. However, testing such assistance is challenging and usually requires real people. The expensive and rare real interaction data leaves a key question unanswered: Can today's MLLMs truly help people in physical world? To answer this question, we propose InteractiveWorld, the first verifiable environment for closed-loop interaction between human and AI assistant. Unlike existing robot-centric simulators, InteractiveWorld lets the assistant guide a human agent who observes the scene, understands instructions, and acts independently. It thus realistically simulates how AI assistant collaborates with human: the assistant instructs, the human acts, and the environment executes actions and updates what they see next. Building on it, we introduce InteractiveBench, the first dynamic benchmark for egocentric AI assistants, with 120 multi-turn tasks across six categories. In each task, the assistant guides the human in real time, and every instruction shapes the outcome, which is scored by verifiable, state-based rewards. Experiments with 12 frontier MLLMs show they are still far from reliable assistants. Even the strongest model, Claude Fable 5.1, achieves at most 20% and 25% on long-horizon Guidance and Planning tasks, respectively. Overall, our work offers a verifiable platform and a rigorous evaluation set, laying a solid foundation for research on interactive MLLM assistants that truly help people in the physical world.
authors: Qinsi Wang, Wei Wen, Chong Zhou, Saksham Suri, Zechun Liu, Lemeng Wu, Hai Helen Li, Yiran Chen, Raghuraman Krishnamoorthi, Qi Qian
bullets: Addresses the difficulty and cost of evaluating egocentric assistants through real human interaction.
Simulates assistant–human collaboration: the assistant instructs, the human acts, and the environment updates accordingly.
Introduces InteractiveBench with 120 multi-turn tasks spanning six categories and state-based rewards.
Evaluates 12 frontier MLLMs; even the strongest model scores at most 20% on Guidance and 25% on Planning tasks.
Provides a platform and benchmark for developing more capable interactive assistants.
papers.selection_reason: Verifiable human-centric environment for evaluating egocentric interactive MLLM assistants; relevant to embodied multimodal assistants.
papers.title: InteractiveWorld: A Verifiable Human-Centric Environment for Building Better Interactive MLLM Assistants
papers.tldr: InteractiveWorld enables verifiable, closed-loop evaluation of MLLM assistants guiding humans through physical-world tasks, revealing that current models remain unreliable.

papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have become strong visual reasoners, yet remain limited in open-world, multi-step search that requires grounding images, selecting tools, and integrating web evidence. Existing approaches typically construct and filter fixed offline corpora whose question distributions cannot adapt as the target deep-search agent improves. Building on MTA-Agent's image-grounded QA construction, we present MTA-Zero, an online multimodal QA-Solver co-training framework for self-improving multimodal deep-search agents that requires no precomputed multi-hop corpus. Starting from image-grounded VQA seed contexts, a trainable QA Generator retrieves evidence and constructs verified multi-hop questions online. A separate deep-search Solver then selects tools, gathers evidence, and answers the generated questions. To focus generation on the Solver's learning frontier, we derive a Goldilocks reward for the QA Generator from the Solver's group-wise rollout success rate: questions solved by all rollouts or by none receive zero reward, whereas questions near the current frontier are favored. We optimize the two policies independently with GRPO, without sharing parameters or gradients. Across six multimodal deep-search benchmarks, MTA-Zero improves a Qwen3-VL-8B Solver from 36.91% to 51.58% mean accuracy and achieves performance comparable to GPT-5 under the same agent workflow. The same framework also improves a newer Qwen3.6-27B Solver by 10.82 points. These results show that verified online question generation provides a policy-specific curriculum for continually improving multimodal deep-search agents.
authors: Xiangyu Peng, Jiaxin Zhang, An Yan, Yu Li, Ran Xu, Zeyuan Chen, Chien-Sheng Wu
bullets: Addresses the rigidity of fixed offline training corpora for open-world, multi-step multimodal search.
Generates verified, image-grounded multi-hop questions online using retrieved evidence.
Uses a Goldilocks reward to prioritize questions at the Solver’s current learning frontier.
Independently trains the QA Generator and deep-search Solver with GRPO, without shared parameters or gradients.
Improves Qwen3-VL-8B from 36.91% to 51.58% mean accuracy across six benchmarks; also boosts Qwen3.6-27B by 10.82 points.
papers.selection_reason: Online co-training framework for self-improving multimodal deep-search agents built on MLLMs; relevant to multimodal LLM agent training.
papers.title: MTA-Zero: Self-Improving Multimodal Deep Search via Online QA-Solver Co-training
papers.tldr: MTA-Zero continually improves multimodal deep-search agents by generating and verifying challenging multi-hop questions online while co-training a question generator and search solver.

papers.abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have demonstrated impressive performance when integrated into robot manipulation pipelines, but real-world evaluation of VLM capabilities on downstream robotics tasks is both difficult and expensive to scale. We propose that spatial and temporal ordering tasks using images from stereo and wrist cameras attached to real-world robots are particularly well-suited for evaluating visual reasoning capabilities, as they assess skills directly applicable to robots. We evaluate VLM reasoning abilities on three questions: ordering shuffled frames conditioned on a language description of the task, ordering objects depthwise based on distance from the camera, and ordering objects from left-to-right in pixel coordinates. The complexity of these tasks can also be modulated by changing the size of the set to sort. Our experiments show that several state-of-the-art vision-language models struggle on ordering tasks. To fix this, we propose a scalable autonomous training data generation pipeline, and show that both supervised finetuning and reinforcement-learning on the generated data can significantly improve VLM reasoning performance both on spatiotemporal ordering tasks as well as downstream robotics and visual reasoning tasks.
authors: Sagnik Anupam, Utkarsh Lal, Aneesh Edara, Botong Zhang, Yao Tang, Jiatao Gu, Dinesh Jayaraman, Osbert Bastani
bullets: Evaluates VLMs on language-conditioned frame ordering, depthwise object ordering, and left-to-right pixel-coordinate ordering.
Uses stereo and wrist-camera images from real-world robots, with task difficulty controlled by the number of items to sort.
Finds that several state-of-the-art VLMs struggle with these robotics-relevant ordering problems.
Introduces an autonomous pipeline for generating scalable training data.
Shows that supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning on this data improve ordering performance and transfer to downstream robotics and visual reasoning tasks.
papers.selection_reason: Improves VLM spatiotemporal and depth-ordering reasoning for robotics via generated data; fits spatial intelligence and embodied reasoning.
papers.title: RoboReason: Boosting Robotics-Relevant VLM Reasoning Through Scalable Data Generation
papers.tldr: RoboReason introduces scalable robot-camera ordering tasks and synthetic training data to improve VLM spatial and temporal reasoning for robotics.

papers.abstract: Embodied perception requires positional representations that capture both physical geometry and the spatial and temporal extent of observations. We introduce POD-RoPE (Physical Observation Distribution RoPE), which represents token observation footprints as distributions over camera centers, viewing directions, and sampling times. Under independent sampling, expected rotations encode relative relationships between distributions; when each distribution collapses to a single address, the construction recovers pointwise RoPE. The same rotation statistics support Q/K matching and coherence-dependent V/O transformations, allowing observation geometry to guide both information selection and content aggregation. Per-token pre-aggregation avoids increasing sequence length or processing pairs of observation nodes. We evaluate POD-RoPE across four robot policy architectures, simulation and real-world manipulation, and complementary reconstruction, depth-estimation, and novel-view-synthesis tasks. Integrating POD-RoPE into Fast-WAM improves mean success from 91.83% to 92.88% across all 50 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks, and from 32.5% to 52.5% on two real-robot tasks on Sharpa North. Controlled reconstruction ablations support the contributions of distribution encoding and V/O transformations. In H20 model-block benchmarks, POD-RoPE achieves median forward-plus-backward speedups of $1.91\times$ over P-RoPE and $5.34\times$ over RayRoPE, with a median latency overhead of 17.4% over Standard RoPE. These results support physical observation distributions as an effective and computationally efficient basis for geometry-aware attention.
authors: Xiaodi Huang, Zilin Wang, Jinpeng Liu, Pengchuan Xiao, Zhenlei Shao, Zhang Zhang, Shuxiang Lu
bullets: Represents each token’s observation footprint as distributions over camera centers, viewing directions, and sampling times.
Uses distribution-derived rotation statistics for geometric Q/K matching and coherence-dependent V/O content aggregation; pointwise RoPE is recovered for single-address observations.
Pre-aggregation incorporates observation geometry without processing pairs of observation nodes or increasing sequence length.
Evaluated across four robot-policy architectures, simulation and real-world manipulation, plus reconstruction, depth estimation, and novel-view synthesis.

Fast-WAM performance improved from 91.83% to 92.88% across 50 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks and from 32.5% to 52.5% on two real-robot tasks; it also outpaced P-RoPE and RayRoPE in H20 benchmarks, with 17.4% median latency overhead over Standard RoPE.
papers.selection_reason: Geometry-aware rotary position encoding for embodied perception and robot policies.
papers.title: POD-RoPE: Rotary Position Encoding over Physical Observation Distributions for Embodied AI
papers.tldr: POD-RoPE encodes the physical extent of embodied observations into attention rotations, improving geometry-aware perception and robot manipulation while avoiding sequence-length growth.

papers.abstract: Many robot manipulation videos do not indicate whether the task was successfully completed. RoboJev-27B is an open-weight vision-language model that takes a task instruction, 10 frames of a manipulation attempt, and (if available) final frames from auxiliary cameras and predicts whether the robot accomplished the task. RoboJev-27B is a variant of JEV-27B-VL, trained with a rank-32 LoRA adapter on the language model only (keeping the vision encoder frozen) using 52,598 episode records. It also uses a source-specific KL penalty that applies only to research data, anchoring predictions closer to the original model on those sources. It uses a calibrated two-token readout that outputs success/failure probabilities in a single forward pass. On 268 held-out episodes of the same robot model (SO-101), RoboJev-27B attains 95.2% balanced accuracy and 0.993 AUROC. It also generalises to episodes collected by unseen labs/robots (AUROC = 0.890 over 459 episodes) as well as to clearly labelled community-collected episodes (accuracy = 93.3% over 135 episodes), where the base model attains an AUROC = 0.900 on the unseen-lab/robot subset with the same inputs. It takes 0.26 seconds per episode (median, serial) to infer on a single H100, which is about \$0.19 per 1,000 success predictions at \$2.69 per GPU-hour (not including media processing and serving costs). RoboJev-27B is released together with its inference code, along with a transparent evaluation: 20,628 predictions organized into 29 model/protocol entries are made available to facilitate browsing and to enable reproducible benchmarking of success detection. We also compare against strong API-based frontier VLMs, which take in fewer input frames (4 images from the primary camera only); note that this comparison is not strictly like-for-like because RoboJev-27B is given more frames at inference.
bullets: Addresses the lack of success labels in many robot manipulation videos.
Fine-tunes JEV-27B-VL with a language-only LoRA adapter, frozen vision encoder, source-specific KL regularization, and a calibrated two-token success/failure readout.
Uses 10 manipulation frames plus optional auxiliary-camera final frames as input.
Reports 95.2% balanced accuracy and 0.993 AUROC on held-out SO-101 episodes; cross-lab/robot AUROC is 0.890.
Released with inference code and 20,628 predictions across 29 evaluation entries for reproducible benchmarking; comparisons with frontier VLMs use fewer frames and are not strictly like-for-like.
papers.selection_reason: Open vision-language judge for robot success detection from manipulation videos.
papers.title: RoboJev: An Open Vision-Language Judge for Robot Success Detection
papers.tldr: RoboJev-27B is an open vision-language model that judges robot manipulation success from task instructions and video frames, achieving strong in-domain and cross-domain performance.

papers.abstract: Whole Slide Image (WSI) analysis serves as the fundamental method for the clinical diagnosis of cancer in digital histopathology. Recent advances in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have enabled state-of-the-art (SOTA) automated histopathology report generation. However, MLLMs reason purely through distributions encoded in their neural parameters, limiting the amount of knowledge and reasoning logic they can contain given the model scale. Their black-box reasoning poses another challenge to the human interpretation of intermediate reasoning. We address these issues by utilizing knowledge graphs to inject external structured knowledge for MLLMs to reason over, while making this reasoning component visible. Knowledge graphs are capable of partially externalizing the containment of medical knowledge, an area that remains underexplored in pathology report generation. We introduce PathKGen, a knowledge graph-assisted MLLM for histopathology report generation. PathKGen has two main branches: (1) a visual path that learns visual token inputs to the MLLM using pathology foundation models, and (2) a knowledge path that learns knowledge token inputs by extracting key morphological features of WSIs through querying a pathology-specific knowledge graph. A comprehensive evaluation on WSI-Bench dataset shows that PathKGen surpasses previous SOTA methods while revealing diagnostic reasoning as visually intuitive graphs. Due to its modular design, the proposed knowledge path is complementary to vision-aligned MLLMs and can be extended to other applications by curating domain-specific knowledge graphs to generate knowledge tokens.
authors: Nadun Rajapaksha, Sandun Herath, Devnith Wijesinghe, Isiri Amani Withanawasam, Hasindri Watawana, Ranga Rodrigo
bullets: Targets limited embedded knowledge and opaque reasoning in MLLMs for whole-slide image analysis.
Uses a visual branch with pathology foundation models to learn visual token inputs.
Uses a knowledge branch that queries a pathology-specific knowledge graph for morphological features and knowledge tokens.
Evaluated on WSI-Bench, where it reportedly surpasses prior state-of-the-art methods and presents reasoning as intuitive graphs.
Its modular knowledge path is designed to complement vision-aligned MLLMs and support other domains with curated knowledge graphs.
papers.selection_reason: Integrates knowledge graphs into an MLLM for explainable histopathology report generation, fitting Multimodal Foundation Models and Language Foundation Models.
papers.title: PathKGen: Pathology Knowledge Assisted MLLM for Explainable Histopathology
papers.tldr: PathKGen improves explainable histopathology report generation by combining visual pathology features with knowledge-graph-derived reasoning tokens in an MLLM.

papers.abstract: Visual token pruning substantially reduces the inference cost of multimodal large language models (MLLMs), yet existing methods are mostly training-free and plug-and-play. They treat the resulting performance drop as an inevitable cost of compression and pursue increasingly complex pruning rules. We rethink this view through two questions: how much of the loss can post-training rescue, and, building on this recovery, how can joint compression push pruning to its limit? We curate a 282K-sample post-training mixture covering general VQA, reasoning, OCR, and grounding, and post-train 36 configurations that drop or merge tokens under a unified protocol. Post-training rescues most of the loss, even for OCR and grounding, and its adaptation gain in closing the gap between the pruned and the dense model grows as the budget tightens. For joint compression, we find that the vision encoder, not the LLM, dominates prefill time in native-resolution MLLMs, so where tokens are removed matters more than how many: keeping 40% of tokens at the encoder runs faster than keeping 10% at the projector. Our best configuration prunes the encoder lightly and the projector aggressively, leaves the LLM intact, and keeps general understanding and reasoning at the dense level. It accelerates the LLM stage by 3.49x but the end-to-end time-to-first-token by only 1.54x, showing that LLM-stage speedups overstate end-to-end gains. We hope these findings offer insights for future research on joint visual token compression. Our data, protocol, and code will be released.
authors: Peiran Yin, Hao Wu, Zihao Yang, Haozhe Hu, Xudong Wang, Xiaoyu Shen
bullets: Post-training largely restores pruning-induced performance loss, including on OCR and grounding tasks.
A 282K-sample mixture spanning VQA, reasoning, OCR, and grounding supports a unified evaluation of 36 compression configurations.
In native-resolution MLLMs, the vision encoder dominates prefill time, making encoder-side pruning more impactful than projector-side pruning.
The best setup lightly prunes the encoder, aggressively prunes the projector, and keeps the LLM unchanged while preserving general understanding and reasoning at dense-model levels.
A 3.49× LLM-stage speedup translates to only a 1.54× end-to-end time-to-first-token improvement.
papers.selection_reason: Rethinks visual token pruning in MLLMs, introducing post-training recovery and joint compression strategies, fitting Efficient AI and Multimodal Foundation Models.
papers.title: Rescuing Your Pruning: Rethinking Visual Token Pruning and Post-Training Recovery in MLLMs
papers.tldr: Post-training can recover most of the accuracy lost to visual token pruning, while pruning location—not just token count—is critical for end-to-end MLLM speed.

papers.abstract: GUI grounding requires locating small controls in cluttered screenshots and identifying which control a natural-language instruction refers to. Cropping and enlargement can expose local detail, but the resulting image may still leave ambiguity about the intended target. We propose PreView, an auxiliary preprocessor that improves the inputs to an existing grounding model without further training that model. PreView prepares two complementary types of input features: task-relevant views for localization and candidate-specific cues for target understanding. A trained lightweight auxiliary model predicts and refines a center, crops the screenshot into a local view, and enlarges that view for zoomed-in grounding. It also prepares a visual cue (i.e., a red-circle marker with a location hint) and a textual cue describing the candidate's identity or function. The frozen grounding model uses the prepared inputs to predict the final click. Across five benchmarks, PreView improves the average grounding accuracy of Qwen3-VL-2B, OS-Atlas-4B, and Qwen3-VL-4B without further training these grounding models. Extensive analyses examine the contributions of views and cues, center refinement, and visual input budgets.
bullets: Targets the difficulty of locating small, ambiguous controls in cluttered GUI screenshots.
Uses a lightweight trained auxiliary model to predict and refine a target center, then crop and enlarge a local view.
Adds candidate-specific cues: a red-circle location marker and text describing the candidate’s identity or function.
Improves average grounding accuracy across five benchmarks for Qwen3-VL-2B, OS-Atlas-4B, and Qwen3-VL-4B without retraining them.
Analyses assess the roles of views, cues, center refinement, and visual input budgets.
papers.selection_reason: Improves GUI grounding for VLMs (Qwen3-VL) using an auxiliary preprocessor that generates task-relevant views and cues, fitting Multimodal Foundation Models.
papers.title: PreView: Enhancing GUI Grounding with Preprocessed Views and Cues
papers.tldr: PreView improves GUI grounding by preprocessing screenshots into localized views and candidate-specific visual/textual cues for a frozen grounding model.

papers.abstract: Attribute-based person retrieval ranks surveillance images from a binary query of semantic attributes, but mean Average Attribute Degree of Match (mADM) drops on unseen cameras as predicted probabilities shift. Common pipelines rank gallery images by their L1 distance to the query, which penalizes a confident single-attribute mismatch no more than small uncertainties across many attributes, while post-hoc recalibration fitted on source validation data fails to transfer because the per-attribute maps fitted on source data do not match those of new cameras. We propose LENS (Likelihood Evaluation and Neighbor Smoothing), combining fine-tuned DINOv3 and CLIP models with a distilled student. LENS regularizes mutually exclusive attribute groups with group cross-entropy in training, scores gallery images by the log-likelihood of the exact query, and smooths gallery logits over nearest neighbors using DINOv3 appearance features from the same forward pass. On held-out datasets, all three changes raise mADM: the likelihood score improves all six retrieval metrics for the main ensemble and mADM for all 48 development models, and training-free kNN smoothing improves all 46 tested development models. On the hidden test set of the UPAR 2027 benchmark, LENS reaches 68.17 mADM.
authors: Nguyen Dang Duy Tan, Vo Thanh Nguyen, Linh T. T. Tran, Huynh Nguyen Phat
bullets: Addresses mADM degradation caused by probability shifts across unseen cameras and limitations of L1-distance ranking.
Uses fine-tuned DINOv3 and CLIP models with a distilled student, plus group cross-entropy for mutually exclusive attributes.
Ranks gallery images by the exact query’s log-likelihood rather than L1 distance.
Smooths gallery logits over appearance-based nearest neighbors using DINOv3 features from the same forward pass.
All evaluated changes improve reported development metrics; LENS achieves 68.17 mADM on the UPAR 2027 hidden test set.
papers.selection_reason: Addresses domain shift in person retrieval using DINOv3 and CLIP, introducing likelihood evaluation and neighbor smoothing, fitting Multimodal Foundation Models and Adaptation and Memory.
papers.title: LENS: Likelihood Evaluation and Neighbor Smoothing for Attribute-Based Person Retrieval on Unseen Cameras
papers.tldr: LENS improves attribute-based person retrieval on unseen cameras by combining likelihood-based ranking, group-aware training, and neighbor smoothing.

papers.abstract: Pedestrian Attribute Recognition (PAR) predicts semantic attributes of individuals, such as gender, age, clothing and accessories, and its descriptions support attribute-based person retrieval and person re-identification. However, accurately recognizing fine-grained attributes across domains remains challenging due to occlusion, appearance variations, and shifts in image distributions. Ensembles of independently trained foundation encoders combine their logits with fixed fusion weights, so every attribute uses the same mix and the encoders are never trained together. We propose UniQuery, which instead jointly fine-tunes DINOv3 and CLIP for attribute-specific fusion. It combines two query heads, one for each encoder, with a joint query head whose attribute queries attend to tokens from both encoders, and the prediction is the average of the logits of the three query heads. We evaluate UniQuery on the benchmark of the UPAR Challenge 2027 at the WACV 2027 Real-World Surveillance workshop, where models are trained on PA100k, PETA and Market-1501 with a shared set of attributes. In leave-one-dataset-out experiments, UniQuery outperforms the independent ensemble in Challenge_Avg on both held-out datasets. Ablations show that learning fusion over independently trained encoders does not improve upon logit averaging in the mean over the two held-out datasets, while freezing the encoders lowers the Challenge_Avg of UniQuery. On the hidden test set of the benchmark, UniQuery achieves a Challenge_Avg of 0.8001.
authors: Nguyen Dang Duy Tan, Linh T. T. Tran, Huynh Nguyen Phat, Vo Thanh Nguyen
bullets: Targets fine-grained pedestrian attributes under occlusion, appearance variation, and domain shift.
Uses separate query heads for DINOv3 and CLIP plus a joint head whose queries attend to both encoders’ tokens.
Averages logits from the three heads for final attribute predictions.
Outperforms an independently trained ensemble in leave-one-dataset-out Challenge_Avg evaluations.
Achieves a Challenge_Avg of 0.8001 on the benchmark’s hidden test set; freezing encoders reduces performance.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes UniQuery to unify DINOv3 and CLIP for cross-domain pedestrian attribute recognition, focusing on joint query heads and fusion strategies for foundation encoders.
papers.title: UniQuery: Unifying Vision Models with a Joint Query Head for Cross-Domain Pedestrian Attribute Recognition
papers.tldr: UniQuery jointly fine-tunes DINOv3 and CLIP with attribute-specific query-based fusion to improve cross-domain pedestrian attribute recognition.

papers.abstract: Pavement crack segmentation under low light is degraded by reduced contrast, shadows, headlight glare, joints, stains, and wet seams. Existing crack segmentation methods mostly assume good illumination. Low-light enhancement methods improve visual quality, but they do not explicitly preserve crack topology. To address these limitations, we formulate low-light crack segmentation as a degradation-aware, prompt-grounded structural defect segmentation problem and propose DROA-CLIPSeg, a parameter-efficient framework that adapts a frozen CLIPSeg vision language backbone using two lightweight modules. QKV Low-Rank Adaptation is injected into the Q/K/V projections of the vision and text encoders to improve crack-specific image text alignment without backbone fine-tuning. The proposed Domain Residual Orthogonal Adapter (DROA) decomposes intermediate features into a dominant crack-domain branch, which captures recurring low-light crack patterns, and an orthogonal residual branch, which preserves faint, thin, and fragmented evidence usually suppressed by noise, shadow, or over-smoothing. We also introduce CrackLingo-9K and CrackLingo-12K, text augmented versions of Crack9k and Crack12k with crack-aware prompts. Training only approximately 1.93 M parameters, corresponding to 1.3% of the full model, DROA-CLIPSeg outperforms 9 zero-shot and 4 fine-tuned vision language baselines on both splits, generalises zero-shot to MVTec AD across textures and defect morphologies, and is supported by extensive ablations. Our source code is publicly available at https://github.com/VShuklacode/DROA-CLIPSeg
authors: Vinita Shukla, Partibha Jangra, Vinayak Pathak, Praful Hambarde, Amit Shukla
bullets: Addresses low contrast, shadows, glare, stains, joints, and wet seams that impair conventional crack segmentation.
Uses QKV low-rank adaptation to improve crack-specific image–text alignment without fine-tuning the backbone.
Introduces a Domain Residual Orthogonal Adapter that separates dominant crack patterns from residual faint, thin, and fragmented evidence.
Provides CrackLingo-9K and CrackLingo-12K, prompt-augmented versions of existing crack datasets.
Reports better performance than 9 zero-shot and 4 fine-tuned vision-language baselines, with zero-shot generalization to MVTec AD; results are limited to the evaluated datasets and settings.
papers.selection_reason: Adapts CLIPSeg for low-light crack segmentation using parameter-efficient adapters (QKV Low-Rank Adaptation, DROA), fitting Multimodal Foundation Models and Efficient AI.
papers.title: DROA-CLIPSeg: Prompt-Guided Thin Crack Segmentation in Low-Light Conditions
papers.tldr: DROA-CLIPSeg enables thin pavement-crack segmentation in low-light imagery by adapting a frozen CLIPSeg model with lightweight, crack-aware modules that preserve faint structural evidence.

papers.abstract: Video spatial reasoning requires multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to understand how objects are arranged and related across viewpoints. While these models can recognize objects in individual frames, integrating these observations to solve complex spatial tasks remains challenging. We examine route planning as a representative task and observe that existing models become substantially less accurate as the number of required turns increases, with several models achieving accuracy close to random guessing on routes requiring three or more turns. This finding suggests that recognizing landmarks alone is insufficient: models must also connect observations across viewpoints and track how landmarks are arranged in a shared space. Motivated by this observation, we introduce GeoLift, a training-free framework that uses feed-forward 3D reconstruction to map objects detected in individual frames into a shared metric 3D scene. GeoLift combines a frozen MLLM for 2D grounding with pretrained geometry models for scene reconstruction. It then uses shared geometric regions, called superpoints, to associate observations of the same object across views without a learned matcher. The reconstructed 3D map enables explicit computation of spatial relations and multistep routes, and provides geometric evidence for estimating distances and sizes. With all model weights frozen, GeoLift improves Qwen3-VL-4B's average score on VSI-Bench from 55.4% to 64.1%, including an increase in route-planning accuracy from 30.9% to 53.6%, and achieves 59.8% accuracy on MindCube. These results show that connecting frame-level object grounding through a shared 3D map can improve complex spatial reasoning without task-specific training.
authors: Xinglin Li, TingTing Long, Jingzhi Zhou, Jiajing Chen, Jian Yang, Jin Xie
bullets: Existing MLLMs struggle to connect landmarks across viewpoints, with accuracy dropping sharply on routes requiring three or more turns.
GeoLift combines a frozen MLLM for 2D grounding with pretrained feed-forward geometry models for training-free 3D reconstruction.
Shared geometric regions called superpoints associate the same objects across views without a learned matcher.
The resulting 3D map supports explicit spatial-relation and multistep-route computation, plus distance and size estimation.
It raises Qwen3-VL-4B’s VSI-Bench average from 55.4% to 64.1% and route-planning accuracy from 30.9% to 53.6%, while reaching 59.8% on MindCube.
papers.selection_reason: Grounds video spatial reasoning in explicit 3D maps, improving MLLM spatial and route reasoning.
papers.title: GeoLift: Grounding Video Spatial Reasoning in Explicit 3D Maps
papers.tldr: GeoLift improves video spatial reasoning by mapping frame-level object detections into an explicit shared 3D scene for multiview route planning and spatial inference.

papers.abstract: Text-to-3D solid retrieval requires aligning natural language with precise geometry despite variations in pose, scale, and recording conventions. Existing methods discretize Boundary Representation (B-rep) models into point clouds or meshes, or learn features from faces, edges, and topology, risking information loss or lacking explicit invariance guarantees. We propose a text-to-B-rep retrieval framework based on group actions and spectral geometric invariants, making invariance an explicit constraint on descriptor construction. Specifically, we use group actions to characterize equivalence transformations induced by translation, rotation, reflection, uniform scaling, and contour recording conventions. For sketch-extrusion solids, we construct a fixed 280-dimensional spectral geometric descriptor by integrating geometric information from three complementary levels, including cross-sectional regions, contour boundaries, and extrusion structures. Furthermore, we use descriptor-consistent multi-positive sets and geometric attribute supervision to promote structural alignment between text and solids. On Text-to-3D solid retrieval, our method achieves 88.6% Recall@5, exceeding the previous state of the art by 13.6 percentage points and demonstrating the effectiveness of explicit geometric invariants for precise 3D solid retrieval.
authors: Hongzhu Yi, Hao Liu, Tao Yu, Tiankun Yang, Yujia Yang, Zhenghao Zhang, Tianyu Zong, Zhenyu Guan, Bingkang Shi, Haopeng Jin, Yuanxiang Wang, Zhongtian Luo, Jungang Xu
bullets: Targets information loss and missing invariance guarantees in point-cloud, mesh, and component-based B-rep representations.
Defines equivalence transformations through group actions, covering translation, rotation, reflection, uniform scaling, and contour conventions.
Builds a fixed 280-dimensional descriptor from cross-sectional regions, contour boundaries, and extrusion structures.
Uses descriptor-consistent multi-positive sets and geometric attribute supervision to improve text–solid structural alignment.
Achieves 88.6% Recall@5, reported as 13.6 percentage points above the previous state of the art.
papers.selection_reason: Text-to-3D retrieval with explicit spectral geometric invariants is directly relevant to spatial and geometric reasoning.
papers.title: Can One Hear Geometry? Gauge-Invariant Spectral Descriptors for Text-to-B-rep Retrieval
papers.tldr: A text-to-B-rep retrieval framework uses explicit spectral geometric invariants to match language with 3D solids despite pose, scale, reflection, and recording variations.

papers.abstract: Advertisers routinely create multiple duration variants of ads to meet marketing budgets and viewer preferences, a labor-intensive and costly process. While multimodal large language models (MLLMs) excel at general video understanding, their ability to perform specialized editorial tasks remains unexplored. We introduce AdShot, a benchmark for evaluating MLLMs on shot selection for ad clipping. It contains 823 professionally edited ad pairs (30-sec sources and 15-sec edits) across 194 brands and 17 industries, annotated with shot-level boundaries and content features (action, emotion, information, imagery). We evaluate 13 state-of-the-art video-only MLLMs and 2 audio-visual MLLMs (7B-72B parameters) on shot selection accuracy (Precision, Recall, F1), duration constraints (15s), and content preservation, including an audio ablation. We find: (1) model architecture matters more than scale, with smaller models often matching or exceeding larger ones; performance is strongest for target ads with 6-10 shots; (2) models exhibit a mean absolute duration error of 5.39s, with most tending to overshoot the 15s target, though they can still substantially reduce human editing effort; (3) all models exhibit systematic content biases, favoring information-rich and emotion-focused shots while under-selecting action and imagery. We publicly release our benchmark to facilitate research at the intersection of multimodal AI and computational advertising.
authors: Wen Xie, Om Rastogi, Sai Siddhartha Vivek Dhir Rangoju, Gijs Overgoor, Yakov Bart, Sarah Ostadabbas
bullets: Addresses the costly, labor-intensive creation of multiple ad-duration variants.
Introduces 823 professionally edited 30-to-15-second ad pairs spanning 194 brands and 17 industries, with shot-level annotations.
Evaluates 13 video-only and 2 audio-visual MLLMs on shot selection, 15-second duration compliance, and content preservation.
Architecture appears more important than model scale; performance is strongest on ads containing 6–10 shots.
Models typically overshoot the target by 5.39 seconds on average, favor information- and emotion-rich shots, and under-select action and imagery.
papers.selection_reason: Benchmark for MLLMs on video shot selection, relevant to multimodal LLMs and video understanding.
papers.title: AdShot: Benchmarking Multimodal Large Language Models for Video Advertisement Clipping
papers.tldr: AdShot benchmarks how well multimodal LLMs select shots to create 15-second ad edits, revealing substantial duration errors and systematic content-selection biases.

papers.abstract: Visual effects are often easier to demonstrate via reference than to describe in words. We study effect-reference editing, where a reference image shows a desired visual effect and language identifies which properties should guide the edit. Existing single-pass editing techniques often fail to make fine-grained edits, resulting in unintended changes to source content or deviations from the reference effect. We introduce KINESYS, a test-time adaptation framework for effect-reference editing that combines reference-aware and source-aware feedback to transfer the desired effect while preserving the composition and content of the original shot. To ensure KINESYS can produce a diverse set of edits that preserve the source, we develop a robust optimization strategy in which the generative model is fine-tuned across multiple noise samples and optimization runs. Evaluation with VLM judges, source preservation metrics (LPIPS, TPIPS), and a user study shows that KINESYS outperforms state-of-the-art image editors in source preservation; on effect transfer, it remains competitive with Nano Banana 2 and outperforms open-weight editors.
authors: Noah Frahm, Luchao Qi, Haoze Li, Dan B Goldman, Sambit Bhattacharya, Roni Sengupta
bullets: Targets fine-grained effect-reference editing guided by both a reference image and language.
Combines reference-aware and source-aware feedback during optimization.
Fine-tunes across multiple noise samples and optimization runs to produce diverse, source-preserving edits.
Evaluations using VLM judges, preservation metrics, and a user study show stronger source preservation than existing editors.
Effect transfer is competitive with Nano Banana 2 and better than open-weight editors.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces KINESYS, a test-time adaptation framework for reference-based image editing that updates the model during inference, fitting test-time learning and multimodal LLMs.
papers.title: KINESYS: Test-Time Adaptation for Reference-Based Effect Editing in Images
papers.tldr: KINESYS uses test-time adaptation to transfer visual effects from a reference image while preserving the source image’s content and composition.

papers.abstract: Visual grounding (VG) in visual question answering (VQA) is a fundamental capability of Vision-Language Models (VLMs), enabling the detection of the most relevant region in an image to answer the question. This reflects the model's capability of multimodal comprehension, which is crucial when interacting with visually impaired people (VIP). Indeed, visual grounding, when applied to assistive scenarios, is not merely a technical feature, but rather a trust and safety requirement. In this work, we study visual grounding in VLMs for visually impaired people. To this end, we assess open-source VLMs on visual grounding using the VizWiz-VQA-Grounding dataset and challenge, which contains real-life images taken by VIP. We propose VG-SHAP, which extends an existing explainability framework to provide visual grounding explanations, allowing the evaluation of black-box VLMs. Our results on the VizWiz-VQA-Grounding challenge show that despite generating correct answers, VLMs struggle to ground in the proper region in the image. However, these results are constrained by the quality of the segmentation model of our explainability framework and further research is necessary.
authors: Fairooz Azim, Lydia Achour, Claudia Borg, Lina Rojas-Barahona
bullets: Visual grounding is framed as a trust and safety requirement for assistive VQA, not merely a technical capability.
The authors evaluate open-source VLMs on the VizWiz-VQA-Grounding dataset and challenge, built from real-life images captured by visually impaired people.
VG-SHAP extends an explainability framework to generate visual grounding explanations for evaluating black-box VLMs.
Results show a disconnect between answer correctness and grounding accuracy.
Evaluation is limited by the quality of the framework’s segmentation model, motivating further research.
papers.selection_reason: Evaluates and explains VLM visual grounding; relevant to spatial intelligence in multimodal models.
papers.title: Evaluating Visual Language Models on Visual Grounding for Visually Impaired People
papers.tldr: The study finds that open-source vision-language models can answer questions about images from visually impaired users but often fail to identify the correct visual evidence.

papers.abstract: Multimodal knowledge editing aims to update visually grounded facts in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) while preserving unrelated text and visual behaviors. However, standard answer-level metrics can hide evidence misgrounding: an edit may produce the target answer on the original image yet remain sensitive to incidental context rather than the intended visual evidence. To examine this issue in a controlled setting, we construct WaterBird-Edit, an analysis set that decouples bird habitat labels from background context and measures whether edited predictions remain stable when the target evidence is preserved but the background changes. Motivated by this diagnosis, we propose VICE (Visual In-Context Editing), a retrieval-based framework that stores edits in external memory and applies them through visual in-context demonstrations designed to expose task-relevant evidence. Experiments on three standard benchmarks show that VICE achieves strong lifelong editing performance, while results on WaterBird-Edit show that it substantially reduces sensitivity to the controlled background shifts. Code and dataset are available in https://github.com/Wang-Z-W/VICE-main.
authors: Zhiwu Wang, Yichen Wu, Jinqian Yang, Yizhou Yang, Renzhen Wang, Qian Zhao, Deyu Meng
bullets: Identifies evidence misgrounding as a failure mode hidden by answer-level editing metrics.
Introduces WaterBird-Edit, which tests prediction stability when target evidence is preserved but background context changes.
Proposes VICE, a retrieval-based external-memory framework using visual in-context demonstrations to highlight relevant evidence.
Reports strong lifelong editing performance on three standard benchmarks.
WaterBird-Edit results show reduced sensitivity to controlled background shifts.
papers.selection_reason: Multimodal knowledge editing with external memory; relevant to MLLM adaptation and continual learning.
papers.title: Diagnosing and Mitigating Evidence Misgrounding in Multimodal Knowledge Editing
papers.tldr: The paper reveals that multimodal knowledge edits can rely on incidental visual context and introduces VICE to make edited predictions better grounded in the intended evidence.

papers.abstract: Unified large multimodal models (ULMMs) are able to perform visual reasoning through interleaved text-image generation, but generating explicit intermediate images incurs significant computational overhead. While visual latent reasoning addresses this, most existing methods rely on vision-language models (VLMs) incapable of visual generation. We propose Oddin, a novel framework enabling latent visual reasoning in ULMMs. Oddin replaces intermediate images with compact latent tokens processed entirely by the understanding branch, reserving the generation branch for the final output image. We train the model via offline self-distillation with three objectives, final image generation losses, text distillation losses, and cross-entropy losses for special tokens. Oddin surpasses interleaved generation baselines and closed-source VLMs on average across seven VBVR-Pro visual reasoning tasks. Qualitative analysis reveals that latent tokens attend to relevant regions in an input image, demonstrating that ULMMs can perform complex visual reasoning without generating intermediate images.
authors: Jaeyong Ko, Hankyeol Kim, Pilsung Kang
bullets: Targets the computational overhead of interleaved text-image reasoning.
Uses latent tokens processed by the model’s understanding branch, while reserving image generation for the final output.
Trains through offline self-distillation combining image-generation, text-distillation, and special-token objectives.
Outperforms interleaved-generation baselines and closed-source VLMs on average across seven VBVR-Pro tasks.
Latent tokens attend to relevant image regions, supporting their role in complex visual reasoning.
papers.selection_reason: Presents latent visual reasoning in unified multimodal models via self-distillation, directly relevant to multimodal large language models and visual reasoning.
papers.title: Oddin: Latent Visual Reasoning in Unified Multimodal Models via Self-Distillation from Image Generation
papers.tldr: Oddin enables efficient visual reasoning in unified multimodal models by replacing intermediate generated images with compact latent tokens.

papers.abstract: While Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have revolutionized general visual perception, existing methods suffer from severe hallucination in the aerial domain, where extreme scale variations and visual ambiguity abound. Existing Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) paradigms force models to mimic ground truth without modeling uncertainty, often resulting in blind guessing on tiny or unrecognizable objects in aerial scenes. In this paper, we present Aerial-R1, the first aerial MLLM framework to reinforce visual reasoning capabilities for aerial reasoning and segmentation. Drawing inspiration from the reasoning-incentivizing mechanisms of DeepSeek-R1, we find that trustworthy perception stems from consistency across views, establishing a visual parallel to the Chain-of-Thought in logic. To effectively adapt policy optimization for non-autoregressive mask generation, we introduce Hybrid-View Group Advantage-Weighted Regression (H-GAWR). This strategy constructs dynamic groups of high-resolution and low-resolution views, seamlessly bridging group-relative advantage estimation with advantage-weighted policy extraction. By enforcing consensus on clear inputs and strictly penalizing hallucinations on ambiguous ones, Aerial-R1 develops an explicitly incentivized refusal mechanism. Extensive experiments on VSAI-Ref, the first aerial MLLM benchmark dedicated to jointly evaluating dense reasoning and hallucination robustness, demonstrate that Aerial-R1 significantly outperforms SFT baselines in segmentation precision while substantially mitigating fatal hallucinations in low-information scenarios, paving the way for more reliable and trustworthy aerial agents. Codes are available on https://github.com/phy709/Aerial-R1.
authors: Jisheng Dang, Huaiyuan Peng, Yixuan Wang, Kun Wang, Zhang Li, Tat-Seng Chua
bullets: Targets severe hallucinations caused by scale variation, visual ambiguity, and SFT’s lack of uncertainty modeling in aerial imagery.
Uses Hybrid-View Group Advantage-Weighted Regression (H-GAWR) to optimize non-autoregressive mask generation across high- and low-resolution views.
Encourages agreement on clear inputs while learning to refuse predictions for ambiguous or unrecognizable objects.
Evaluated on VSAI-Ref, where it reportedly surpasses SFT baselines in segmentation precision and reduces hallucinations in low-information scenarios.
papers.selection_reason: Aerial MLLM with reinforcement-style reasoning and segmentation, reducing hallucination.
papers.title: Aerial-R1: Reinforcing Aerial Reasoning and Segmentation in MLLMs
papers.tldr: Aerial-R1 improves aerial image reasoning and segmentation by reinforcing cross-view consistency and penalizing hallucinations, especially for ambiguous or low-information scenes.

papers.abstract: Embodied vision-language models must answer questions from partial, evolving observations. Their success depends on both the reasoning capability selected and the evidence available to it. Expert routers adapt internal computation, while tool-augmented systems acquire external evidence; choosing these independently can leave a suitable expert without the evidence it needs. We introduce EKT-Router, a bounded framework that jointly selects a capability expert, optional knowledge, and perceptual tools. Outcome-derived signatures represent the overlapping strengths of General, Spatial Reasoning, and Spatiotemporal experts. A joint utility scores complete expert-evidence routes under a call budget. After acquisition, a packet verifier admits valid evidence with positive predicted expert-conditioned gain. The selected expert then answers once, reverting to the unchanged observation if all packets are rejected. Across 6 embodied QA benchmarks, EKT-Router achieves a mean score of 61.4, the highest among the compared systems, and averages 74.7 on 10 general vision-language benchmarks. With all external evidence disabled, question-conditioned expert selection alone improves over the best fixed expert by 1.75 points. Ablations show that learned routing is the dominant component and that knowledge and perception are complementary.
authors: Weilin Ruan, Yingjie Xu, Yangkai Wei, Bohan Zhou, Shuaibo Li, Harold Haodong Chen, Kaiwen Zhou, Yinchuan Li, Ying-Cong Chen, James Cheng
bullets: Addresses the mismatch between selected reasoning capability and available evidence in partial, evolving observations.
Uses outcome-derived expert signatures for General, Spatial Reasoning, and Spatiotemporal experts.
Scores complete expert–knowledge–perception routes under a call budget, then verifies evidence for expert-conditioned usefulness.
Achieves a mean score of 61.4 across 6 embodied QA benchmarks and 74.7 across 10 general vision-language benchmarks.
Expert selection alone improves 1.75 points over the best fixed expert; ablations identify learned routing as dominant and knowledge and perception as complementary.
papers.selection_reason: Joint expert-evidence routing for embodied vision-language models, improving embodied QA.
papers.title: EKT-Router: Expert-Evidence Alignment for Embodied Vision-Language Models
papers.tldr: EKT-Router jointly selects reasoning experts and external evidence to improve embodied and general vision-language question answering under limited tool calls.

papers.abstract: Short-form video combines speech, imagery, and on-screen text, creating challenges for systematic content analysis. We present a five-stage multimodal framework for measuring creators' themes and communication strategies at scale. The framework integrates platform metadata, speech transcripts, and vision-language descriptions of sampled frames, then applies large language models to generate predefined indicators and open-ended labels. An audited keyword scheme consolidates thematic labels, while creator-weighted aggregation gives each account equal weight regardless of posting volume. We demonstrate the framework on 9,852 TikTok videos from sixteen creators, retaining 7,311 videos for analysis across seven themes and seven communication indicators. Automated profiles reveal substantial differences in creators' use of education, humor, and responses to current events. Validation against two independent expert annotators yielded a mean framework-expert agreement of Cohen's $\kappa = 0.40$ across the six binary indicators, close to the $\kappa = 0.42$ the two experts achieved with each other, though agreement varied substantially across individual indicators. The framework provides a modular approach to comparative analysis of creator communication, combining scalable annotation with transparent aggregation and construct-specific validation.
authors: Julie R. Ancis, Michael Fire, Omer Tarshish
bullets: Addresses the challenge of systematically analyzing speech, imagery, and on-screen text in short-form video.
Combines platform metadata, transcripts, sampled-frame descriptions, LLM-generated indicators, and audited thematic labels.
Uses creator-weighted aggregation so accounts contribute equally regardless of posting volume.
Demonstrated on TikTok videos from 16 creators, identifying differences in education, humor, and responses to current events.
Expert validation showed moderate agreement overall, with performance varying substantially by indicator.
papers.selection_reason: Presents a multimodal framework for analyzing short-form video using LLMs, relevant to video understanding and multimodal analysis.
papers.title: A Multimodal Framework for Measuring Creator Communication on Short-Form Video
papers.tldr: A scalable multimodal framework analyzes short-form video creators’ themes and communication strategies using metadata, speech, visuals, and language models.

papers.abstract: We introduce Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB, a hybrid Mamba-Transformer vision-language model that optimizes speed and intelligence per GB of memory used for local agentic workloads. Derived from the Nemotron 3.5 Super VL 120B-A12B model family, Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB combines Star Elastic compression with 2-bit Quantization-Aware Distillation for memory-constrained deployment. The model is optimized for reasoning, agentic tool use, and web & terminal interactions. We also trained a LiLiCorr speculative drafter that is released alongside the model to reach our target inference speed. The resulting model achieves a higher accuracy than leading models with similar memory footprints and speed across many benchmarks for general agentic capabilities (e.g., GDPVal v2), web browsing (e.g., BrowseComp), and terminal use (e.g., Terminal-Bench 2.1), with a relatively high TPS of 84 on RTX Spark that is comparable to models with much lower active parameter counts and more than sufficient for long-horizon agentic applications.

papers.selection_reason: Hybrid vision-language model optimized for local memory-constrained deployment with compression and speculative decoding.
papers.title: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB: A Hybrid Vision-Language Model for Local AI
papers.tldr: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB is a compressed hybrid vision-language model designed for fast, capable local agentic AI under tight memory limits.

papers.abstract: Speaking-style captioning (SSC) aims to generate natural language descriptions of how speech is delivered, capturing paralinguistic attributes such as vocal timbre, prosody, and expressivity. Many downstream applications, including conversational AI agents, controllable speech generation, and large-scale audio annotation, require dimension-specific style captions that describe targeted aspects of speech (e.g., speaker traits, emotion, or delivery style), rather than a single undifferentiated description. However, existing work lacks a unified formulation for controllable speaking-style captioning. We address this gap by formulating SSC as an instruction-following audio-language task, where explicit instructions specify the speaking-style dimensions to be described. We introduce StyleInstructCaps, the first standardized benchmark for controllable speaking-style captioning in audio-language models. StyleInstructCaps provides a dataset and evaluation framework that measures metadata groundedness, hallucination, instruction-following ability, generalization to unseen instructions and audio datasets, and speaker-style consistency. Across nine state-of-the-art audio-language models, we find that strong instruction-following ability does not necessarily imply grounded speaking-style understanding, and that SSC-specific instruction-diverse training substantially improves groundedness, controllability, and speaker consistency.
authors: Shreeram Suresh Chandra, Ashwyn Sharma, Liang Lu, Xiutian Zhao, Leda Sari, Bj\"orn Schuller, Berrak Sisman
bullets: Frames speaking-style captioning as an instruction-following audio-language task targeting dimensions such as speaker traits, emotion, and delivery style.
Introduces a standardized dataset and evaluation framework for groundedness, hallucination, instruction following, generalization, and speaker-style consistency.
Evaluates nine state-of-the-art audio-language models.
Finds that instruction-following strength does not guarantee grounded speaking-style understanding.
Shows that instruction-diverse SSC training improves groundedness, controllability, and speaker consistency.
papers.selection_reason: Benchmark for controllable speaking-style captioning in audio-language models, relevant to multimodal LLM instruction following.
papers.title: A Benchmark for Controllable Speaking-Style Captioning in Audio-Language Models
papers.tldr: StyleInstructCaps benchmarks whether audio-language models can generate grounded, instruction-controlled descriptions of specific speaking styles.

papers.abstract: As multimodal large language models (MLLMs) reason for longer, attention to the initial visual input diminishes, weakening visual grounding. Visual memory reintroduces visual evidence during reasoning. We conduct a controlled analysis of visual memory along three axes: curation, organization, and access. We find that local evidence benefits from global context, compact latent representations balance accuracy and visual-context cost, and the utility of memory access depends on the reasoning state. Guided by these findings, we propose ReMAP (Reasoning-Time Memory-Augmented Perception), which couples two complementary latent memories: a static, question-conditioned Global memory that preserves scene and cross-image context, and a dynamic Local memory that uses this context as an anchor while selecting and re-encoding region-level evidence according to the current reasoning state. Both memories return compact latent tokens inserted into the reasoning sequence, and a reinforcement-learning access policy trained with branched rollouts decides when to continue reasoning or invoke Global or Local memory. On ten benchmark families, ReMAP outperforms prior visual-memory methods on all four multi-image benchmarks, exceeding the strongest prior results on MuirBench and MIMIC by 8.38 and 14.84 percentage points. Across four backbone families, enabling memory access improves over the same trained model with memory disabled, and on shared V*Bench, CV-Bench-2D, and MuirBench questions ReMAP reduces the visual tokens entering the reasoning sequence by 51.0-76.8% relative to the native-resolution backbone. Further analyses show that Global and Local memory form distinct yet complementary latent representations. Together, these components restore the perceptual cycle by letting the reasoning state trigger targeted visual retrieval, with the retrieved evidence guiding subsequent reasoning.
bullets: Long reasoning can diminish attention to the initial visual input, motivating visual memory during inference.
ReMAP combines a question-conditioned static Global memory with a reasoning-state-dependent dynamic Local memory.
A reinforcement-learning policy decides whether to continue reasoning or access either memory.
It outperforms prior visual-memory methods across all four multi-image benchmarks, with gains of 8.38 and 14.84 percentage points on MuirBench and MIMIC.
Memory access reduces visual tokens entering the reasoning sequence by 51.0–76.8% on shared benchmarks, while Global and Local memories provide complementary representations.
papers.selection_reason: Reasoning-time latent visual memory for MLLMs that restores visual grounding and reduces visual tokens.
papers.title: ReMAP: Restoring the Perceptual Cycle with Reasoning-Time Latent Visual Memory
papers.tldr: ReMAP restores visual grounding in long MLLM reasoning by dynamically retrieving compact global or local visual memories when needed.

papers.abstract: Semantic misinformation can arise when an authentic image is paired with a caption that changes or distorts its narrative. Because the image itself may contain no visible signs of manipulation, methods designed to detect pixel-level artifacts can miss these misleading image-caption pairs. We study this problem using DGM4+, a dataset designed to evaluate the detection of global scene and semantic inconsistencies. We propose a multimodal model that combines image-text representations from SigLIP with visual scene features from DINOv2 through a projection MLP, and adapts Qwen2-VL-7B using LoRA. The model jointly predicts whether an image-caption pair is authentic, identifies the manipulation type, and grounds the misleading caption tokens. On the DGM4+ validation split, the model achieves an F1 score of $0.9679$ for binary authenticity classification. These results suggest that parameter-efficient adaptation of vision-language models is promising for detecting semantic inconsistencies, while also motivating further work on precise token-level grounding.
bullets: Targets global scene and semantic inconsistencies that pixel-level manipulation detectors may miss.
Combines SigLIP image-text representations with DINOv2 visual scene features through a projection MLP.
Uses LoRA to adapt Qwen2-VL-7B for joint authenticity classification, manipulation-type prediction, and token grounding.
Achieves an F1 score of 0.9679 for binary authenticity classification on the DGM4+ validation split.
Token-level grounding remains an area for further improvement.
papers.selection_reason: Adapts a multimodal foundation model for image-caption authenticity detection and token-level grounding, fitting multimodal large-language-model understanding.
papers.title: MiD-VLM: Detecting and Grounding Global Semantic Misinformation in Image-Caption Pairs
papers.tldr: MiD-VLM detects semantic misinformation in authentic image-caption pairs and grounds the misleading caption tokens.

papers.abstract: We introduce RynnUnify, a 16B unified embodied model that combines strong embodied understanding with long-horizon visual planning through interleaved video--language reasoning. With capabilities spanning spatial reasoning, physical prediction, and grounding, RynnUnify connects an understanding of the physical world with visual anticipation of how it evolves across successive subtasks. Building on these capabilities, we further develop an agentic extension through reinforcement learning to selectively use video predictions for reasoning about unobserved states and interaction outcomes. We also develop a world-action extension of the full RynnUnify model, translating its understanding and prediction capabilities into robot control. To evaluate these capabilities, we introduce Rynn-VP and Rynn-GEU for long-horizon visual planning and anticipatory reasoning. Experiments show that RynnUnify achieves the highest average embodied understanding score among the evaluated unified multimodal models and improves the Rynn-VP overall score by 9.75 points over Cosmos 3 Nano. Its agentic extension improves the Rynn-GEU average by 6.0 points over direct reasoning, while the world-action extension achieves 51.5\% success on 20 selected composite RoboCasa365 tasks and 46.7\% average success across three real-robot tasks. Together, these results establish RynnUnify as a shared foundation for embodied understanding, visual planning, and robot control, taking a step toward a unified embodied brain.
authors: Minghao Zhu, Bohan Hou, Kun Xiang, Zixuan Wang, Yinzhou Tang, Yifei Yang, Zhikai Wang, Tianyi Zhang, Kehan Li, Haoyu Zhao, Siteng Huang, Leigang Qu, Sicong Leng, Dongchi Huang, Mingxiu Chen, Shijian Lu, Yue Wang, Xiaodan Liang, Zhenyu Zeng, Deli Zhao, Chengju Liu, Jianfei Yang, Xin Li
bullets: Supports spatial reasoning, physical prediction, grounding, and anticipation of evolving scenes across subtasks.
An agentic reinforcement-learning extension selectively uses video predictions to reason about unobserved states and interaction outcomes.
A world-action extension translates the model’s understanding and prediction capabilities into robot control.
The model achieves the highest average embodied-understanding score among evaluated unified multimodal models and improves Rynn-VP by 9.75 points over Cosmos 3 Nano.
Its extensions improve Rynn-GEU by 6.0 points over direct reasoning and achieve 51.5% success on selected RoboCasa365 tasks and 46.7% average success across three real-robot tasks.
papers.selection_reason: Unified embodied model combining video-language reasoning, spatial understanding, visual planning, and robot control spans multiple configured topics.
papers.title: RynnUnify: Towards Unified Embodied Brain
papers.tldr: RynnUnify is a 16B unified embodied model that combines physical-world understanding, long-horizon visual planning, and robot control through interleaved video-language reasoning.

papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning for large language models often uses separate systems for inference and training. Even with identical weights and BF16 tensors, implementation differences can make an intended on-policy update off-policy and destabilize training. Existing remedies align the entire inference and training stacks, change global precision, or modify the learning algorithm. We ask whether aligning selected parts of the execution stack can stabilize BF16 RL while other implementation differences remain. We align training-side rounding locations with inference in three regions---RoPE, SwiGLU, and residual RMSNorm---by retaining selected intermediates in FP32 until their BF16 outputs. Across four Qwen-family models, aligning all three regions prevents the collapse observed under the default BF16 baseline; RoPE-path alignment alone also suffices in the studied runs, despite remaining numerical discrepancies. The interventions keep the inference engine, matrix-multiplication and attention kernels, and learning objective unchanged.
authors: Yijing Ke, Tianle Cai, Ruosong Wang
bullets: Implementation differences between inference and training can make nominally on-policy RL updates effectively off-policy and destabilize training.
The study aligns training-side rounding locations with inference in RoPE, SwiGLU, and residual RMSNorm.
Across four Qwen-family models, aligning all three regions prevents collapse seen with the default BF16 baseline.
RoPE-path alignment alone suffices in the studied runs despite other numerical discrepancies.
The interventions leave inference, matrix-multiplication and attention kernels, and the learning objective unchanged.
papers.selection_reason: Investigates numerical stability in LLM Reinforcement Learning by aligning rounding locations in the execution stack, preventing training collapse.
papers.title: Where Rounding Happens Matters: Rounding-Location Alignment Stabilizes LLM Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: Aligning where rounding occurs between inference and training can stabilize BF16 reinforcement learning for LLMs without changing the inference engine or learning objective.

papers.abstract: Objective: To develop a unified vision-language model for prompt-conditioned quantitative ultrasound measurement that addresses the mismatch between continuous measurement targets and discrete token-based numerical prediction. Methods: This article presents HAD-VLM, a hybrid autoregressive-diffusion framework that combines autoregressive text generation with continuous measurement prediction within a shared backbone. Visual prompt tuning adapts the vision encoder to ultrasound images. A diffusion process predicts a five-component representation comprising caliper endpoint coordinates and measurement length. A post-processing strategy combining the proposed coordinate-length consistency mechanism with ensemble prediction is introduced to refine measurement estimates. We evaluate four echocardiographic measurement tasks on EchoNet-LVH, with additional assessments of medical question answering and X-ray vertebral measurement. Results: HAD-VLM achieves mean absolute errors of 1.36, 2.77, 3.05, and 1.16 mm for IVSd, LVIDd, LVIDs, and LVPWd, respectively, reducing errors by 21.4-37.6\% relative to the Vicuna-based autoregressive baseline. It also outperforms fine-tuned Qwen3-VL and direct MLP regression across all four tasks. Medical question answering performance is preserved on the evaluated dataset. For X-ray vertebral measurement, HAD-VLM reduces mean absolute error from 11.4 to 6.7 pixels.
